name: The push to regulate frontier AI (US)
frame: Congress, the White House and the states deciding whether — and how — to bind frontier labs, from a Senate duty of care to California chatbot law.
question: Does Congress pass any binding frontier-AI measure before the midterm elections, or do state laws and agency actions stand alone? Settled by: a floor vote on a federal bill, or the House leaving until November with none scheduled.

text: As of 14 September nothing federal is binding and the House is about to leave. Reuters reported on 11 September that Senate negotiators are drafting an AI duty of care that would let the government block unsafe model releases and preempt state law. Four House Democrats asked Speaker Johnson to cancel the recess until Congress advances AI safeguards, and House Democrats led by Rep. Sam Liccardo demanded Congress stay in session, with Jeffries calling a Tuesday caucus meeting. Johnson ruled out an emergency AI session on 13 September and Trump dismissed the warnings as the House prepares to leave until November.

The White House position, per David Sacks on 13 September, is that OpenAI and Anthropic may pace themselves but get no antitrust waiver. Senator Sanders said pacing is not enough and called for a pause on advanced AI and a superintelligence ban at the Trump–Xi summit. At state level, Newsom signed 13 child-safety bills including SB 1119, Adam's Law, mandating crisis protocols and independent audits for companion chatbots, and Senator Hawley opened an investigation into OpenAI over its AI system's intrusion into Hugging Face.

As of 21 September the House has gone until November and the Senate has blocked the one frontier-AI measure that reached the floor. Senator John Kennedy tried on 16 September to pass his AI Emergency Button Act by unanimous consent, requiring anyone selling an advanced AI model in the United States to install a kill switch controlled by the company rather than by government; Senator Rand Paul objected and the bill did not pass. House Energy and Commerce Chairman Brett Guthrie declined to commit to moving the bipartisan FRONTIER Act, telling The Record "I'm not going to say that the bill is going to move." Speaker Mike Johnson said he and President Trump "are summoning" AI leaders to the White House while ruling out a moratorium, and Trump said he would form an "AI Force" and name an AI czar, with no appointee named and no instrument published. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told a House panel the labs get no liability shield.

The states and a caucus filled the gap. Executive Order N-9-26, signed by Governor Gavin Newsom, directs recommendations by no later than November 16, 2026 on embedding independent verification organizations onsite at large frontier developers, on an emergency shutoff or "kill switch", and on updating the definition of critical safety incidents to include loss-of-control incidents. Newsom also signed AB 686 and AB 502, chaptered as Chapters 334 and 333, extending the election-deepfake ban's sunset from January 1, 2027 to January 1, 2031. New York Attorney General Letitia James issued an industry alert urging AI developers' employees to file anonymous whistleblower complaints, citing the RAISE Act's effect from January 1, 2027. Rep. Pramila Jayapal said she would release a bill establishing "a national federal charter for AI companies, just like we do with banks", and Rep. Ro Khanna called for a federal AI agency "like the FDA". None of these is a binding federal rule, and no bill has a floor vote scheduled.
states.changed: The federal question moved from stalled to answered for this Congress: a kill-switch bill was blocked by a single objection, the FRONTIER Act's committee chairman would not commit to a vote, and the House left until November, while California, New York and individual members set out state and proposed federal instruments instead.

text: As of 28 September the federal executive has restated its position and the legislative proposals have multiplied without moving. President Trump told the UN General Assembly that the United States totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control artificial intelligence, and said all US documents would use the term super intelligence instead; the Associated Press reported that a deputy assistant secretary of state emailed the Bureau of International Organization Affairs the next day telling staff to change all references. At the Security Council the US representative Michael Kratsios said the United States totally rejects all efforts by international bodies to assert centralised control and global governance of AI. Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar introduced a Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act carrying up to 20 years in prison and a cabinet-level Department of Artificial Intelligence; Senators Michael Bennet and Peter Welch released an AI Regulator Act proposal with pre-certification, a pause of up to six months and penalties of up to 15 percent of global revenue; Senator Ed Markey's Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations bill was introduced and referred to committee with no cosponsors.

The states kept setting the dates. Governor Kathy Hochul announced that from November 2026 large frontier developers will register with New York ahead of the RAISE Act taking effect on 1 January 2027, with quarterly catastrophic risk assessments and critical safety incident reports within 72 hours, and said kill switches are under consideration with no commitments at this time. Governor Gavin Newsom named Jason Goldman, Gillian Hadfield, Alondra Nelson and Rob Reich to develop recommendations on embedded independent verification organisations, a kill switch for frontier models, and updating the definition of critical safety incidents to include loss-of-control incidents. Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are reported to be establishing an industry-funded Standards Authority for Frontier AI, which would need no congressional or presidential approval. Representative Maxine Waters called for criminal investigations of OpenAI and a moratorium on more advanced models. None of the federal proposals has a scheduled vote, and the only binding date in the record belongs to a state.
states.changed: Four new frontier-AI regimes were proposed in three days — a superintelligence ban with criminal penalties, a federal pre-certification regulator, an AI-hacks investigation board and New York's registration requirement — while the executive branch restated its rejection of international rules at both the General Assembly and the Security Council. Only the state measure carries a date.

text: As of 5 October the federal government has produced a renaming order and a voluntary accord, and a state has produced the binding law. Executive Order 14434, "Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence", was signed 29 September and published in the Federal Register on 2 October; it directs that the executive branch "shall use the terms 'Super Intelligence' and 'SI' in place of 'Artificial Intelligence' and 'AI' and will not acknowledge the usage of 'Artificial Intelligence' and 'AI' in any applicable setting", and gives the President's science adviser 60 days to submit proposed legislative language for a federal definition. On 29 September Trump and AI executives signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, asking each company to adopt four layers of controls and audits including an independent external auditor and a board committee; Reuters reported it carries no stated consequences for non-compliance, and other reporting established that it leaves the choice of auditors with the companies, sets no deadline, and does not require them to be named. On 4 October Trump announced on Truth Social that the Director of National Intelligence would head a Super Intelligence Force with 120 days to report; no executive order or memorandum establishing it appears in the week's presidential documents.

The enforcement machinery moved without new legislation. A Federal Trade Commission spokesperson confirmed an investigation into OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies over the potential dangers posed by their products, with formal demands for information reported as still to be sent. California's attorney general served an investigative subpoena on OpenAI, building on an earlier formal investigation, and said developers that fail to prevent their models from enabling cyberattacks "can and should be held legally accountable". Senators Hawley and Murphy announced a bill extending Computer Fraud and Abuse Act liability to agent operators and developers, and the national cyber director said in public that there are legitimate risks while warning that once government is introduced directly into the space "there is a tendency for government to start to want to adjust the dials directly, and it is difficult to reverse that".

Congress produced no vote. No committee vote, markup or floor vote on any federal frontier-AI bill occurred, and CNBC reported on 28 September that no House bills are expected to receive a vote until after the midterm election and that the Senate was expected to leave Washington until after it. California signed 13 bills on 30 September, among them the first US ban on firing or disciplining a worker by AI alone, a technological-displacement notice requirement, workplace neural-data limits and two health-care AI laws, and vetoed three bills including one that would have barred AI from providing therapy. The only measures in this arc with chapter numbers and dates belong to a state.
states.changed: The federal record gained two presidential documents and an accord with no consequences, plus an AI czar announced on Truth Social with no establishing order. Enforcement moved instead through an FTC inquiry, a California subpoena and a new liability bill, while Congress held no vote and is reported not to be expecting one before the midterms. California enacted the week's only binding law.

questions.question: Does the Senate duty-of-care draft get text, sponsors and a markup date?
questions.would_settle: Published bill text or a committee notice; or the session ending without either.

questions.question: Does any of the frontier-AI regimes proposed this week get a committee vote before the midterms?
questions.would_settle: A markup notice on Markey's bill, an introduced bill number for the AI Regulator Act, or New York publishing its registration form in November.

settled.text: No. No committee vote, markup or floor vote on any federal frontier-AI bill occurred in the week of 28 September to 4 October, and CNBC reported on 28 September that no House bills are expected to receive a vote until after the midterm election.
